belief: If I pray enough, I shouldn’t need a doctor or counselor.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if you pray enough you shouldn’t need a doctor or counselor, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that seeking medical or psychological help shows weak faith. Stories of healing through prayer alone. Fear of what others at church would think. Distrust of doctors or counselors. Pride or embarrassment about needing help.
teaches: Prayer and practical help go together in Scripture. James tells the sick to call the elders to pray over them and anoint them with oil, which in that time was also used as medicine. The Good Samaritan bandaged wounds with oil and wine. Luke was a beloved physician. Jesus said the sick need a doctor. Praying and seeking care are not opposites; God often answers prayer through doctors and counselors.
self_statements: If I pray enough, I won’t need help.
Seeing a doctor means I don’t trust God.
Counseling is for people with weak faith.
God will be disappointed if I get treatment.
Taking medicine is giving up on God.
errors: Believing you must choose between prayer and help.
“I should be able to pray this away.”
Overlooking examples of prayer and care together.
Accepting help for some problems but not others.
questions: What did James tell the sick to do besides pray?
How did the Good Samaritan care for the wounded man?
What did Jesus say about who needs a doctor?
Could God answer my prayers through a doctor or counselor?
Would I tell a friend with a broken bone to only pray?
Is my hesitation about faith, or about fear or pride?
What help might God be offering me right now?
truth: Praying and getting help are not opposites. God often answers prayer through doctors, counselors, and medicine. I can pray with faith and also seek wise care. Seeking help is good stewardship of the life God gave me, not a lack of faith.
hw_questions: What did James say besides pray?
How did the Good Samaritan help?
Who needs a doctor, according to Jesus?
Could God answer through a doctor?
Would I tell a friend to only pray?
What help is God offering me now?
hw_truths: Prayer and practical help go together.
God often answers prayer through doctors and counselors.
I can pray with faith and get care.
The sick need a doctor, and that is no shame.
log: Each day, write one prayer for my health and one practical step I took to care for it.
name_example: And the prayer offered in faith will restore Sarah when she is sick. The Lord will raise her up.
actions: then make one appointment you’ve been putting off.
Ask your church elders or a pastor to pray for you,
and tell them about any treatment you’re receiving.
and write how the Samaritan combined compassion and care.
Write your fears about getting help,
and answer each with a truth from this card.
tracker: One prayer and one step of care
prayer: Father, thank You that You hear my prayers and that You often answer through people You have gifted to heal. Help me reject the lie that if I pray enough, I shouldn’t need a doctor or counselor. Give me humility to seek help and faith to trust You through it. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
